ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan: Money Laundering Control Act (MLCA) as amended, Company Act (Articles 386-1 and 387-1) requiring UBO registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), and Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) regulations on AML/CFT. For the Chinese parent entity, PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective Nov 1, 2024) mandates UBO disclosure at Government_Only_Access level. The JV in Taiwan must comply with Taiwan's AML/CFT framework while ensuring the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) information of the Chinese parent is disclosed only to government authorities, not publicly.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Chinese Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China is a member of the Apostille Convention since Nov 7, 2023) - obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China, then submit to the Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) for verification (notarization and legalization).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Chinese Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (as above) followed by TECO verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Taiwan JV formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chinese Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese notary public, then Hague Apostille, then TECO verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Chinese Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (as above) followed by TECO verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Chinese Parent's primary bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Chinese notary public, then Hague Apostille, then TECO verification.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the following lists: (1) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) List; (2) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) Taiwan's Ministry of Justice Anti-Money Laundering Division's list of designated persons and entities; (5) China's Ministry of Public Security list of sanctioned individuals and entities. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP (Politically Exposed Persons) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations, including domestic and international PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least annually), and upon any trigger event (e.g., change in ownership). All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Automated screening tools with fuzzy matching algorithms must be used to identify potential matches, and any positive hit must be escalated to the compliance officer for review and risk mitigation. The protocol must also include negative news screening and adverse media checks for all UBOs and senior management.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Commerce - Company Name Pre-Approval System (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be registered as a secondary name, but the Chinese name is the legal name. The name must consist of a distinctive part, a business type (e.g., 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.'), and may include a geographic or industry descriptor. Phonetic transliteration from foreign languages is permitted but must be approved by the MOEA. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name; (2) it must not contain prohibited or sensitive words; (3) it must not be misleading as to the nature of the business; (4) it must comply with the Company Act and related regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be in writing, stating the grounds for appeal and providing evidence that the name is not confusingly similar or prohibited. The MOEA will review the appeal within 30 days and issue a final decision. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a further administrative lawsuit with the Taipei High Administrative Court within 30 days. During the appeal process, the applicant may submit a revised name application without prejudice. It is recommended to conduct a preliminary name search on the MOEA portal and to consult with a local attorney to avoid common pitfalls.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Single Family Office (SFO) engaged in private investment holding, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible. Taiwan's tax authorities (National Taxation Bureau) and banking institutions require a physical registered office where records are kept, board meetings can be held, and regulatory inspections can be conducted. The Company Act mandates that a company must have a registered office within Taiwan, and the address must be a physical location where the company's statutory books and seals are maintained. Banks, when opening corporate accounts, will conduct on-site visits to verify the physical presence. A virtual office may be acceptable for administrative purposes but will not satisfy the 'place of effective management' test for tax residency and may trigger enhanced scrutiny. Therefore, a physical office lease is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered office must have a visible company name plate; (2) Statutory books (share register, minutes, etc.) must be available on-site; (3) A designated company secretary or representative must be present during business hours; (4) The office must have a dedicated telephone line and mail reception; (5) The office must not be a mere virtual address or shared mailbox. Risk: The likelihood of unannounced physical inspections by the MOEA or the National Taxation Bureau is moderate (estimated 20-30% annually) for investment holding companies, especially those with foreign shareholders. Inspections are more frequent if the company is flagged for unusual transactions or if the registered office is in a low-cost business center. To mitigate risk, maintain a fully staffed office and ensure all statutory records are up-to-date.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act, Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 12, 128, 129, 131, 156, 172, 203, 208, 222, 387 and 393; the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4 and 8; and the Money Laundering Control Act applicable to investment holding and family office entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Taiwan Company Registration One-Stop Service).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form and Registration Declaration for Establishments of Companies Limited by Shares, filed under Article 387 of the Taiwan Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None as a statutory floor. Taiwan does not impose a minimum paid-in capital amount for a company limited by shares. However, the subscribed capital must be fully paid into a Taiwanese bank account and substantiated by a bank-issued paid-in capital certificate before filing. Foreign-invested capital must first be approved by the Investment Commission, MOEA, and remitted through the approved foreign exchange route. The capital is not held in a blocked escrow account unless a specific condition in the investment approval letter so provides.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association tabled at this meeting, substantially in the form attached and initialed by each director for identification, be and the same are hereby approved and adopted for filing with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the Company is hereby authorized to proceed accordingly; (2) that the authorized share capital of the Company be fixed at NTD [fill amount] divided into [fill number] ordinary shares with a par value of NTD [fill amount] each, and that the paid-in capital immediately upon subscription shall amount to NTD [fill amount], being not less than the amount declared in the incorporation application; (3) that the directors and subscribers approve the allotment of shares as set out in the share subscription schedule, and the Chairperson is directed to issue share certificates accordingly, and to credit contributed capital to a company capital account at a licensed Taiwanese bank, such capital being earmarked for lawful company purposes and not for immediate refund; (4) that the registered office of the Company be and it is hereby fixed at [full address in Taiwan], and the directors are instructed to file the adopted address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and to execute any notarized consent of the premises owner if so required; (5) that the directors be and they are hereby authorized to open, maintain and operate banking accounts with [private bank] and any domestic authorized financial institution, and to designate authorized signatories jointly to sign checks, accept deposits, transfer funds, execute securities custody agreements, and sign foreign exchange settlement forms, and to provide such powers of attorney and specimen signatures as the bank may require; (6) that [Name] is appointed as Chairperson, [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Statutory Auditor of the Company, each to serve according to the Articles and until replacement, and that such officers are authorized to sign incorporation declarations and statutory returns; and (7) that the officers be directed to apply for all required corporate tax, labor insurance, and investment commission filings, and to take all steps necessary to obtain the certificate of incorporation and Uniform Company Number from the competent authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-clearance of company name and foreign investment approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan) and the MOEA Company Name Pre-Application System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant shall first submit a company name and business scope pre-application through the MOEA one-stop online portal. Simultaneously, the foreign investing shareholder must file an investment application with the Investment Commission, specifying the proposed shareholding percentage, source of remittance, capital account structure, and the single-family office business purpose. The application shall include notarized corporate resolutions of the foreign parent company and evidence that the proposed activity does not sit on a restricted list. The Investment Commission will issue an approval letter fixing the approved foreign currency amount and remittance schedule. No capital may be remitted into Taiwan until the approval letter is issued. The pre-approved name must be used in all subsequent constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Company name pre-application form
Investment Commission application form
Notarized foreign shareholder board resolution
Power of attorney executed in favor of local representative
Single-family office business plan and source of funds declaration
Remittance schedule and bank reference letter
Copy of parent company certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or suspension, supplementary explanations and corrected documents may be uploaded through the online portal within 14 days. If a formal rejection is issued, the applicant may file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public or court-affiliated notary office authorized by the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating shareholders shall prepare and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the share subscription schedule, the first board minutes, and the registered office consent letter. All foreign-language corporate resolutions must be accompanied by a notarized English or Chinese translation for filing with the Taiwan registry. The signatories must appear before a Taiwan notary or submit duly certified copies through a qualified attorney. The Articles must express the limited liability nature, share class, investment holding purpose, appointment and removal mechanism of directors, quorum requirements, and indemnification provisions. The notarized first board resolution must be consistent with the pro-forma resolution adopted for share subscription, bank account opening, registered office, and officer appointment.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Share subscription schedule
Pro-forma first board resolution
Registered office consent and lease or title document
Notarized identification documents of directors and shareholders
Foreign language board resolution with notarized translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the documents for correction, the parties may re-execute signatures and resubmit with a supplementary notarial certificate within seven days. If the translation is defective, a new conformed notarized translation must be filed before the incorporation application is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan Company Registration One-Stop Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant shall file the incorporation application online through the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Service using the approved company name. The filing package must include the notarized Articles, first board resolution, share subscription list, bank certificate of paid-in capital, Investment Commission approval, registered office evidence, and identification of all directors. The registry will verify capital payment, corporate governance compliance, statutory officer validity, and name consistency. Upon successful verification, the authority issues the Company Registration Certificate and the Uniform Company Number. The company must then prepare its company seal and corporate resolution book for subsequent use in banking and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Online incorporation application form
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
First board resolution minutes
Bank paid-in capital certificate
Investment Commission approval letter
Registered office consent and supporting address documents
Identification cards or passports of directors
Article 387 registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice, the applicant may cure the omissions within 15 days. If the application is suspended for unpaid fees or inconsistent translations, the applicant may pay the required fee and resubmit a corrected package. A formal rejection may be contested by administrative appeal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, AML compliance, labor registration, and banking activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Financial Supervisory Commission Taiwan; Labor Insurance Administration; and the chosen private bank compliance department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must register with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and obtain a tax payer number. If no taxable sales are conducted initially, the company shall file an identity certificate application and will be included in the tax declaration roster. Under the Money Laundering Control Act, the company operating as a single-family office investment holding entity shall adopt a written AML risk assessment, customer due diligence policy, beneficial ownership verification, and suspicious transaction reporting procedure. The company must also register as an employing unit with the Labor Insurance Administration if staff are hired. Finally, the directors shall activate the private bank and securities custody accounts using the Company Registration Certificate and approved signatory matrix.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate / Uniform Company Number
Taxation registration application form
Corporate seal and signatory specimen cards
AML compliance policy and risk assessment
Beneficial ownership and source of funds declaration for shareholder-owners
Private bank account opening package and custody agreement
Labor insurance and health insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If taxation or AML registration is delayed, a rectification filing may be made with any applicable penalty relief under the Tax Collection Act and Money Laundering Control Act. If the private bank rejects the account opening for AML concerns, the company may provide enhanced source-of-wealth evidence and a revised signatory matrix within 10 business days or file a complaint through the Financial Ombudsman system.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - pure office-based single-family office and private investment holding activity under ISIC 6430; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or construction project triggering the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, no VOC emission sources, no stationary combustion equipment, and no hazardous waste generation at the registered office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no factory premises, no hazardous substance storage, and no covered industrial establishment under the Fire Services Act. If an ordinary office lease is executed, the landlord must provide a valid building safety certificate and the company must maintain a workplace safety supervisor in compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for general office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), administered by the National Taxation Bureau having territorial jurisdiction; online business registration and filing via the Ministry of Finance Tax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw), with company and UBN registration co-administered by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commercial Affairs and foreign-investment screening by the Investment Commission where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested or joint-venture entity, the procedure is: (1) obtain foreign-investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs where the foreign shareholding triggers approval; (2) incorporate the limited company or branch/representative office under the Company Act in the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commercial Affairs database, thereby obtaining the statutory Unified Business Number (UBN) which serves as the tax/VAT identifier; (3) complete business tax registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing operations by submitting the incorporation documents, UBN certificate, registered address proof, business scope, and director/shareholder disclosure; (4) for non-resident enterprises without a fixed place of business in Taiwan, apply separately to the National Taxation Bureau for a non-resident taxpayer registration through the Ministry of Finance Tax Portal for withholding-tax and VAT obligations on Taiwanese-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not have a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch pass-through election; profit-seeking enterprises are taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act. Group taxation is available only on a statutorily qualified consolidated-loss basis, not as an elective pass-through or hybrid regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (value-added and non-value-added tax regime under the Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for incorporated profit-seeking enterprises: registration is mandatory before commencing business. For small-scale business operators, simplified taxation applies when monthly sales remain below NT$80,000 for goods or NT$40,000 for services, but such threshold does not apply to a limited liability joint-venture family office vehicle registered as a VAT-taxable business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must issue uniform business invoices in accordance with the Uniform Invoice Use Regulations. Approved electronic-invoice taxpayers must use Ministry of Finance-certified e-invoicing systems, transmit invoice data through the turnkey API to the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform, and comply with time-stamped transmission and retention requirements; the platform performs the anti-fraud digital clearance and exchange functions. Failure to transmit on time or issuing non-compliant invoices is penalized under the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating eligibility under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act covers: (i) goods exported from Taiwan with customs declaration; (ii) goods or services supplied to a foreign buyer and used outside Taiwan; and (iii) qualifying services rendered in Taiwan for offshore customers, including offshore digital or financial back-office services, provided the taxpayer proves the export/supply, retains the contractual and invoice documentation, and evidences collection of consideration in foreign currency or NT dollars from overseas in compliance with Central Bank of China (Taiwan) foreign-exchange regulations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Customs Bill of Entry/export manifest) filed with Taiwan Customs
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill issued by the commercial carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or, for Taiwan bank evidence, the bank-issued foreign-exchange receipt statement evidencing repatriation of export proceeds from a foreign client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau may re-examine all zero-rated export transactions and will disallow the 0% rate if the export documents, customs clearance, shipping evidence, or foreign-exchange repatriation proof are incomplete or not received within the required period. Disallowed amounts are subject to retrospective assessment of 5% business tax plus interest; where false documentation, fictitious exports, or fraudulent refund claims are involved, the taxpayer faces a deficiency penalty of up to five times the evaded tax, potential criminal tax-evasion liability for responsible officers, and forfeiture of any VAT refund previously granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), jointly with the Financial Supervisory Commission for banking and capital-market licensing
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime rather than a fully free float. The New Taiwan Dollar is convertible on current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, interest and ordinary remittance, without a prior exchange-control permit, although all settlements must pass through a CBC-authorized bank and be reported under thresholds in the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act. Capital-account flows, including inbound equity investment from a mainland Chinese shareholder into the Taiwan JV, remain controlled and are subject to prior authorization, investment filing, and bank-level FX declaration; they are not freely convertible on demand. Export proceeds do not have to be surrendered to the central bank, but the exporter must evidence collection within statutory timelines and may retain them in foreign currency deposit accounts. Profit remittance can be blocked by unresolved tax clearance, CRS classification mismatches or source-of-wealth deficiencies, but routine dividend distributions with audited financial statements and withholding tax proof are honored. The jurisdiction is therefore best described as partially convertible: liberal on trade and operating liquidity, restrictive and documentary-intensive on capital movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must complete an Export Transaction Declaration (ETD) through an authorized bank within 10 working days after customs shipment and must collect the foreign exchange proceeds within 180 days from shipment. There is no mandatory surrender ratio under the current liberalized regime: 0% of export receipts must be converted where the company elects to retain a foreign-currency deposit; if converted to NTD, the effective conversion amount is 100% of the claimed remittance at prevailing market rates. All collection and conversion must be reported to the CBC and authorized bank under the Foreign Exchange Transaction Reporting Rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and Private Banking Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. A pure fintech EMI without a Taiwanese banking license cannot legally open NTD clearing accounts, hold client custody assets, or service the SFO as a primary treasury counterparty. Foreign EMIs may be accepted only as technology or white-label intermediaries routed through a licensed domestic bank; the legal account relationship remains with the FSC-licensed bank and the CBC-regulated depository institution. Any proposal to use an offshore EMI as the operating bank must therefore be rejected for statutory compliance reasons.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the standard first-time corporate account opening requirement in Taiwan. The actual responsible person must attend the branch in person, or a locally appointed officer may appear with a notarized power of attorney endorsed by the Taiwanese board resolution. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for full-service NTD accounts; a video call may be used only as an additional verification layer, not as a substitute. Some private banks will accept the legal representative of the JV if the ultimate beneficial owner completes a separate confirmation interview, but complete digital onboarding is not available for this entity class.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership layers across the single-family office, trust structure and multiple cross-border intermediate holding vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified organizational chart showing every direct and indirect owner through to the individual natural persons, the trust deed and all amendments, the register of shareholders and directors, passport copies of settlor, protector and beneficiaries, tax-residency certificates, CRS self-certifications, and a personal-source-of-wealth statement prepared by the family office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound CNY-denominated capital injection from the mainland Chinese shareholder into the Taiwan JV without a clear regulatory path
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved cross-strait investment filing or applicable FSC/CBC approval documentation, board resolutions approving the capital call, the shareholder loan or equity subscription agreement, source-of-funds letters from the remitting bank, audited financial statements of the parent for the last three years, and a funds-flow narrative reconciling the exact remittance amount to approved capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6430 private investment holding with no active commercial trading creates enhanced underwriting exposure for the bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The family office constitutive contract or trust management mandate, investment policy and minutes of the investment committee, custody account statements from a licensed Taiwanese securities or private bank, a portfolio snapshot showing the assets under management, and an independent AML/CTF risk assessment confirming neither tax evasion nor sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the FX declaration purpose code and the actual economic activity of the remittance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exact Foreign Exchange Transaction Declaration codes quoted on the bank application, the underlying contract or investment agreement for each wire, the settlement advice, the commercial invoice or board capital resolution, and evidence of withholding tax or corporate tax filing for any dividend or profit-remittance leg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or the local equivalent from the remitting bank to the designated Taiwan bank beneficiary account. The remittance instruction must state EQUITY INJECTION FOR CN_JV_LTD and include the receiving bank's settlement code. The bank requires a completed Inward Remittance Application for Equity Investment, the capital subscription resolution, the investment approval or cross-strait filing, and CBC Foreign Exchange Transaction Declaration forms. After settlement, the bank issues a foreign exchange certificate, the company obtains a CPA capital verification report, and the amount is registered with the relevant corporate registry within the statutory timeline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements may be executed through SWIFT MT103 for direct high-value payments, MT700 for commercial letters of credit funding cross-border imports or exports, and documentary collections (MT400/MT202) for lower-value settlement. All NTD legs must clear through the Taiwan domestic interbank system; USD and other foreign-currency legs can be cleared through CHIPS, Fedwire or the correspondent network of the authorized domestic bank. No outgoing remittance may bypass a licensed CBC bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign-exchange contracts with a licensed Taiwanese bank for committed current-account trade or service cash flows, tenor not exceeding 180 days and supported by invoices or contracts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the SFO has genuine offshore underlying FX exposure and the local bank maintains central-bank reporting; speculative NDFs without documented exposure are disallowed.

Cross-currency swaps permitted for confirmed foreign-currency loan or bond obligations, subject to CBC registration when maturity exceeds one year, accounting hedge documentation and no speculative leverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved board-prepared business report, financial statements, and profit distribution/loss compensation proposal, together with the shareholders' meeting approval record and subsequent copy filing with MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration and Management Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders' meeting must be convened within six months after fiscal year end (June 30 for a calendar-year company); the approved balance sheet and income statement must be filed with MOEA within fifteen days after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the approved statements renders the responsible person liable to an administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000, with repeated renewal until compliance; if the company has not commenced business for six months or has ceased business for six months, MOEA may issue an administrative strike-off order under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual settlement return (including securities/gain schedules and net asset schedules relevant to the SFO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (local administration office), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers file between May 1 and May 31 of the following year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, filing is due within five months of fiscal year end (six months when the return is CPA-attested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late tax payment adds a surcharge of 1% for every two days of delay up to 15%, after which the case is transferred to compulsory execution. Late or non-filing after statutory notice triggers a deemed assessment and an additional tax under Income Tax Act Article 108; proven tax evasion is penalized under Article 110 up to three times the tax evaded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register annual review and unconditional MOEA update filing when any covered change occurs (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The board must annually review and date the in-house Article 22-1 beneficial ownership register at the final board meeting; any change in a principal shareholder (10% or more), director, senior manager, or ultimate beneficial owner must be filed with MOEA within fifteen days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A responsible person who fails to file or maintain the beneficial-ownership register is subject to an NT$10,000–NT$50,000 administrative fine, renewable on continued non-compliance; false or concealed beneficial ownership data may also attract Money Laundering Control Act penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax returns and income withholding statements for salaries, director fees, consulting fees, and Taiwan-source payments to recipients, where the SFO acts as an employer or payer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Withholding statements for the prior calendar year must be delivered and filed by January 31 of the following year; withholding remittances are due on the statutory 10th-of-month / payment-event schedule for the relevant withholding period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing exposes the withholding agent to administrative fines under Income Tax Act Article 114 and Tax Collection Act late-filing/late-payment surcharges; intentional false withholding statements can be penalized up to twice the withheld amount.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A licensed independent CPA audit is mandatory when the Taiwan entity is a public company, a bank/insurance/securities enterprise, or another Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC)-regulated institution; or when it meets any quantitative threshold set for non-public companies: paid-in capital exceeding NT$30,000,000; annual net operating revenue exceeding NT$50,000,000; total assets exceeding NT$50,000,000; or regular headcount exceeding 100 employees. A single-family office that stays below all thresholds is not subject to a compulsory CPA audit, but lenders, private banks, and custodians may still require audited or reviewed financials before extending credit or executing custody agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public-interest entities and financial institutions must apply Taiwan-IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the FSC). Private unlisted companies must prepare financial statements under the Commercial Accounting Act, applying the Enterprise Accounting Standard (EAS) / Taiwan GAAP, or elect full Taiwan-IFRS if approved by MOEA. The family office must prepare consolidated statements if it controls investment subsidiaries or underlying operating entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the company must keep a current beneficial-ownership register listing principal shareholders (normal threshold: 10% or more), directors, managers, and ultimate beneficial owners, and must file any change with MOEA within fifteen days; Taiwan does not operate a separate annual UBO confirmation filing, so the board documents an annual review and reconciliation of that register in the final board meeting minutes. For share transfers in a private unlisted company, the transfer is effective against the company only when recorded in the Register of Members; Taiwan does not impose a uniform 30-day regulator-reporting window for private share transfers. A delay in the register entry may suspend voting/dividend rights until corrected and may trigger the 15-day MOEA update requirement if the transfer changes beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges / Mortgages and share pledges
Minute Book containing shareholders' and board meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$650 – US$2,200 per year for a registered office and professional statutory agent in Taipei
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 – US$12,000 per year for a low-volume single-family office audit under EAS/Taiwan GAAP

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan grants a 5-year tax holiday for qualifying newly established Free Trade Zone enterprises and certain strategic industries; profit-seeking enterprise income tax basic deduction of NT$120,000 for small and medium enterprises; research and development expenditure deduction up to 15% of qualifying R&D costs (provided the taxpayer files an advance application and maintains contemporaneous documentation); no patent box regime applicable to a Single Family Office holding passive investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 99) filed through the Ministry of Finance Tax Administration Network Tax Filing System (e-Filing).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment due by the 5th month after the end of the fiscal year (usually 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers); extension of one additional month may be applied for before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue and business income derived from Taiwan sources, including management fees received by the Single Family Office for family asset administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Taiwan-source revenue derived from services rendered or assets located in Taiwan, including fees for private banking advisory services, investment advisory mandates, and administrative services to related family companies. Unreported Taiwan-source management fees constitute a high-risk omission subject to underreporting penalties and criminal fraud referrals if intentional.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, including eligible dividend income subject to the imputation system and gains from sale of qualifying securities where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include dividend income actually received from ROC-domiciled investee companies that qualify for the participation exemption (ownership of 20% or more and held for at least one year). Non-resident shareholders should note that the participation exemption is generally unavailable to non-resident shareholders not conducting substantial business in Taiwan; absence of Economic Substance may trigger reclassification as taxable business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of revenue and allocable direct expenses; for a Single Family Office, amortization of acquired private equity fund management rights, salaries of investment professionals, and occupancy costs used for family office operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by valid vouchers and may be allocated between Taiwanese and offshore activities on a reasonable cost allocation basis. No deduction is allowed for expenses incurred in earning tax-exempt income; a pro-rata disallowance must be computed. Intra-group management fee payments must satisfy the arm's length requirement and be supported by a transfer pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryforward and investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Taiwanese branch or subsidiary of a non-resident family investment holding structure, taxable net income is limited to Taiwan-source income after allowable deductions. Apportionment of global head-office expenses is permitted only with the approval of the local tax authority; otherwise, the full disallowance applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward from prior 10 years (subject to the minimum tax regime and ownership continuity requirement).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is allowed only if the company continues the same business and the corporate shareholders holding more than 50% of the shares remain unchanged; an indirect transfer of the Taiwan JV by a non-resident parent through offshore restructuring may invalidate the carryforward. The enterprise must file a formal loss carryforward schedule with reconciliation to the audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, investment credits, and foreign tax credits; computation of Income Tax Basic Amount (Alternative Minimum Tax) for the Single Family Office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are capped by the Taiwan tax attributable to the foreign-source income. Unilateral tax credit may be claimed only if the non-resident jurisdiction qualifies under the rules of the Income Tax Act, and DTA relief may override domestic credit provisions. For offshore family investment vehicles, ensure that all investment gains attributable to Taiwan financial assets are declared; otherwise the Ministry of Finance may impose a 20% delinquent tax surcharge and refer for criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to penal interest at the postal savings rate compounded daily from the original due date; late payment incurs an additional 1% every 30 days up to 10% of the unpaid amount. Intentional filing of a false return with the purpose of evading tax is punished under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act with a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax, and under Article 109 of the Tax Evasion Penalty Act, imprisonment for up to five years, a fine of NT$30,000 to NT$900,000, and confiscation of undeclared profits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% for non-resident corporate shareholders (withholding at source upon distribution); 28% for non-resident individuals.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced withholding rate under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, complete Form A (Application for Treaty Relief), and file a beneficial ownership declaration demonstrating no pass-through arrangement. The Taiwan withholding agent must send the application to the National Taxation Bureau before the dividend distribution date. The beneficial owner must prove it has substance (minimum staff, premises, and active management) and is not a shell conduit. Absolute blacklist violations include filing false TRCs, submitting forged beneficial ownership declarations, and circumventing Article 6 of the Income Tax Act by routing dividends through a no-tax intermediary.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% on royalties paid to non-residents and 15% on interest paid to non-residents. DTA relief generally reduces the royalty rate to 10% and interest to 10%, subject to the same TRC and beneficial ownership proof. For a Single Family Office holding intellectual property or providing intercompany loans to the Taiwan JV, the Taiwan tax authorities will scrutinize whether the IP is developed and managed in Taiwan; any royalty or interest payment without economic substance will be recharacterized as a taxable dividend at the higher statutory withholding rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Taiwan Dollar (NTD) 50 million for intercompany transactions; transfer pricing Local File and Master File are mandatory when annual related-party revenue exceeds NT$50 million or overseas related-party transactions exceed NT$20 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Taiwan tax authority applies the Economic Substance Doctrine through the anti-avoidance rule in Article 12-1 of the Income Tax Act, disregarding arrangements lacking commercial substance. A Single Family Office is expected to have a minimum number of qualified employees, an office in Taiwan, a substantive business purpose, and a decision-making capability over asset acquisitions and dispositions. If the family office is deemed not to conduct Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Taiwan, its passive investment income may be reclassified as Taiwanese-source business income, attracting a 20% corporate income tax plus surcharge and, where fraud is evident, criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Undeclared Offshore Investment Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Single Family Office, through its Taiwan JV entity, receives advisory fees in Taiwan but routes the economic benefit to a Hong Kong or BVI shell without reporting the offshore investment income to the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau, or falsely declares the family office as a pure passive holding company with no Taiwanese employees when in fact it manages assets and executes agreements in Taipei.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 110 of the Income Tax Act imposes a fine of up to three times the evaded tax, plus a 20% delinquent tax surcharge. Article 109 of the Tax Evasion Penalty Act prescribes imprisonment for up to five years for willful evasion; evasion exceeding NT$1 million triggers immediate criminal referral and publication on the tax blacklist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax as well as penalties; civil proceedings may attach personal assets, including family trust distributions. The director may be subject to a travel ban and entry refusal (blacklisting). If tax evasion is proven beyond a reasonable doubt, the director faces imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years with no suspension if the sum exceeds NT$3 million. The court may also disallow the director from being a director of any Taiwan company for 5 years under the Company Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Corporate Form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan JV is registered as a legitimate limited company, but it has no business operations, no staff, no office, and no assets other than intercompany receivables; it exists solely to receive dividends from the Taiwan operating subsidiary and to obtain treaty benefits by routing profits to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 12-1 of the Income Tax Act, the tax authority may disregard the corporate entity and reallocate income to the actual economic owner, levying a 20% corporate income tax on the diverted income, plus an additional 20% penalty for non-arm's length pricing. The company may be struck off under the Statute for Establishment and Management of the Branches of Foreign Companies if it possesses no substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors who knowingly permitted the shell arrangement may be held personally liable for all unpaid corporate tax under the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil; asset preservation orders can freeze personal bank accounts and real property. Directors may be banned from traveling abroad (blacklisted) and from holding board positions in any Taiwanese financial institution for 10 years. If the shell is used to evade tax by paper losses, directors may be criminally charged under Article 41 of the Money Laundering Control Act and face imprisonment of up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Breach for Family Office Investment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Single Family Office processes large wire transfers for private banking and securities custody without filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to the Taiwan Anti-Money Laundering Office, particularly when funds originate from a jurisdiction lacking DTA transparency, or when the beneficial owner keeps changing without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9 of the Money Laundering Control Act imposes a fine of NT$1 million to NT$10 million on the company and its directors who fail to implement internal control and know-your-customer procedures; repeat offenders face a mandatory shutdown of the licensed activity and revocation of the corporate filing. Violation of Article 5 (incomplete customer due diligence) is punished by an administrative fine up to NT$5 million and a public reprimand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable to the state for the unreported transaction under the doctrine of knowing participation; personal assets may be seized, and a travel ban is automatically issued when the criminal investigation is initiated. A conviction for money laundering by a family office director carries imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years and a fine up to NT$5 million; the director also faces permanent disqualification from serving as a trustee or investment advisor in Taiwan. The court may order the forfeiture of the entire SFO asset pool if the funds are traced to unlawful activity.
